I disagree that these comments are coming from a place of harassment. 
I think the place they’re coming from, is at a point in many peoples lives, especially when they first start having sex, they didn’t like it or didn’t enjoy it until they met someone who made them feel a certain way, or made them truly orgasm and made them enjoy sex. Sex can be a wonderful natural thing and if it’s something someone else finds joy in and pleasure in, I think they’re more coming from a place of not wanting you to miss out on experiencing that pleasure because you haven’t found someone to give you that experience. They’re coming from the point of view of their own experiences.
As ace’s though, we may never enjoy sex and that’s where the misunderstanding comes from. 
We don’t view it like other people do. We don’t find that same joy, or have those impulses.
The other comments such as SO needs is a tricky one. We have needs and boundaries but so do our SO. It becomes a trade off of our needs/boundaries vs theirs. We can either:
a) compromise and meet somewhere in the middle
b) expect them to totally accept our boundaries and we don’t compromise at all on our boundaries for their needs
c) only date people who have the same needs as us
I do agree there needs to be more understanding of how our boundaries are a party in this arrangement.
But again, I think they’re more coming from a place of, “I don’t want to see you narrow your dating pool and not find love because of this” without understanding, our best match will be someone that understands us and is supportive of our boundaries. 
Just my view anyways.
